findings.title: Breaking API change: `findMany` method removed without migration path
findings.body: The public `findMany` method that was the primary query interface for consumers of this service has been completely removed and replaced with `getBaseConditions()` which only returns raw SQL conditions. Any existing caller using `service.findMany(...)` will break at compile time. The PR does not show updates to any callers, nor does it provide an equivalent high-level query method. This is a breaking change to the service's public API.

findings.title: Dead code branches in `getBaseConditions` due to always-truthy `authConditions`
findings.body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object (never null or undefined), and `Prisma.Sql` objects are always truthy in JavaScript. Therefore the condition `if (authConditions && filterConditions)` on line 72 effectively only checks `filterConditions`. The `else if (filterConditions)` branch (line 76) and the final `else` branch (line 78) are unreachable dead code. While not a runtime bug, this is misleading and could mask future issues if the return type of `getAuthorizationConditions` changes.

findings.title: Integration test asserts exact result set without isolating from pre-existing data
findings.body: The test `should combine authorization and filter conditions` asserts `expect(results).toEqual([{ id: userBooking.id }])`, expecting exactly one row. If the test database contains other bookings that match the combined conditions (same userId, teamId IS NULL, matching eventTypeId), the test will fail with extra rows. Unlike the old `findMany` test which used Prisma's structured queries with the same isolation concern, this raw query test provides no additional scoping (e.g., by booking UID or creation timestamp) to guarantee isolation from other data.

findings.title: Caching behavior tests removed without replacement
findings.body: The previous test suite included explicit tests verifying that `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` return cached results on subsequent calls. These tests were removed entirely. While the caching logic still exists in the service (lines 84-95 of insightsBooking.ts), there is no test coverage confirming it works correctly with the new `Prisma.Sql` return type, particularly that the cached `Prisma.Sql` object maintains referential or structural equality across calls.
